issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell after driving, coolant drips at the front or back of the engine, and sometimes milky oil or overheating.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 uses plastic-framed lower intake gaskets that break down over time, especially with old coolant. Coolant then leaks outside the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and check the oil for a milky look. Get the gaskets replaced soon, because coolant in the oil can ruin the engine bearings.

issues.t: Head gasket failure
issues.sym: Engine running hot, coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, rough running with a check engine light, or milky oil.
issues.why: Head gaskets on the 3.4L V6 can fail, often after an earlier intake gasket leak or an overheating episode. Owners also report gaskets eaten away by old coolant.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask a shop for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test before more damage is done.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Engine revs flare between gears, the van slips or loses gears, hunts between gears on hills, or stops moving in drive.
issues.why: The automatic transmission in these vans wears internally, and owners report failures from about 25,000 to over 150,000 miles. Some needed more than one rebuild.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not engage, stop hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis. A rebuild or a replacement unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Erratic shifting from pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: Shifts feel harsh, late or random, and the shifting may change from one drive to the next.
issues.why: A failing pressure control solenoid inside the transmission cannot hold line pressure steady. RepairPal lists it as the most reported Montana problem.
issues.next: Have the codes and transmission pressure checked. Replacing the solenoid early can prevent damage that leads to a full rebuild.

issues.t: Power sliding door can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The power sliding door may pop open while the van is moving, mostly on hills, turns or rough roads.
issues.why: GM recalled these vans because the power sliding door could unlatch while driving. Anyone not wearing a seat belt could fall out.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Keep everyone belted until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power sliding door can push a passenger's arm (recall)
issues.sym: If a passenger holds the inside handle while the power door opens, the door can drag their arm into the seat back or armrest.
issues.why: GM recalled about 717,000 of these vans because the power door motor kept pulling the door open against a passenger's grip.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Fuel gauge jumps or reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge swings between full and empty, sticks at one reading, or the low fuel light comes on with fuel in the tank.
issues.why: Owners report erratic gauges at 68,000 to 139,000 miles. The usual cause on GM vans of this age is a worn fuel level sender in the tank, but owners did not confirm a single cause.
issues.next: Track mileage at each fill-up so you don't run dry. A shop can check whether the sender or the gauge is at fault.

issues.t: Overheating with sludge in the cooling system
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, the heater may blow cold, and brown sludge shows up in the radiator or coolant tank.
issues.why: Owners report overheating at around 111,000 miles and sludge in the radiator. Sludge usually comes from old or contaminated coolant, often mixed with oil from a leaking gasket.
issues.next: Don't keep driving an overheating engine. Have the cooling system flushed and checked for a leaking intake or head gasket.

issues.t: Air conditioning stops working
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, or works only some of the time.
issues.why: Owners report A/C failures at about 60,000 miles. The usual causes are a leak, a failing compressor or a bad clutch or relay.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressure-tested and checked for leaks before anyone recharges it, so you know what failed.

issues.t: Climate system keeps running after the van is off
issues.sym: The blower or climate system stays on after you turn off the engine and remove the key, which can drain the battery.
issues.why: Owners report it around 50,000 miles. A climate control module or relay that doesn't switch off is the common suspect.
issues.next: If the fan won't shut off, pull the HVAC fuse overnight to save the battery and have the climate control circuit checked.

issues.t: Front sway bar link breaks
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle over bumps, and the van leans more in turns.
issues.why: Owners report the sway bar or its link breaking near 98,000 miles. Worn links and rusted mounts are common on older vans.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Sway bar links are quick to replace.

issues.t: No heat from the vents
issues.sym: The heater blows cold or barely warm air, especially at idle.
issues.why: Owners report no heat at about 100,000 miles. Low coolant, a stuck thermostat or a clogged heater core are the usual causes.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first with the engine cold. If it's full, have the thermostat and heater core flow checked.

issues.t: Check engine light from a loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the van drives.
issues.why: A gas cap that doesn't seal lets fuel vapor escape, and the evaporative system sets a leak code.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few days of driving, replace the cap and have the code read.

issues.t: Hard start, stalling or no start
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time, needs gas pedal to start, stalls, or won't restart after a short stop. The fuel gauge may jump around too.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for hard starts, stalls and erratic fuel gauges on these vans. Owners say shops often can't reproduce it.
issues.next: Note when it happens (hot, cold, after a short stop) and ask a GM dealer to check the fuel pump module against bulletin 01-08-45-005.

issues.t: Coolant leak from crossover pipe gaskets
issues.sym: Coolant level drops, with a sweet smell or drips near the top front of the engine.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for coolant leaking from the coolant crossover pipe gaskets on the 3.5L and 3.9L V6.
issues.next: Top up the coolant and have the leak traced. Replacing the gaskets is a moderate job, much smaller than fixing an engine that overheated.

issues.t: Head gasket failure on the 3.9L V6
issues.sym: Overheating, weak heat, the A/C shutting off to protect the engine, loss of power and shaking.
issues.why: Owners report head gasket failures on the 3.9L V6 at about 43,000 to 57,000 miles, letting coolant leak out or into the cylinders.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test done.

issues.t: Power steering clunk, knock or whine
issues.sym: A clunk or knock when turning, or a loud groan or whine from the steering, especially in cold weather.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for power steering clunk on these vans and for steering noise in very cold weather. One 2007 owner needed all the steering lines replaced.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Have a shop find the noise before a hose or pump fails.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsation when stopping
issues.sym: The brake pedal or steering wheel shakes when you brake.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for brake pulsation from uneven front rotors and replaced the front brake shields as part of the fix.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured. They usually need refinishing or replacing along with new pads.

issues.t: Reduced engine power warning
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a reduced engine power message, and the van barely accelerates.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this condition that replaces the throttle position sensor cover on the throttle body.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask a GM dealer about bulletin 12-06-04-003A before replacing the whole throttle body.

issues.t: Oil leak at the side of the oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the van and oil wetness along the side of the oil pan.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for diagnosing and repairing oil leaks on the side of the oil pan on these engines.
issues.next: Keep the oil level up and have the leak traced. Resealing the pan is usually enough.

issues.t: Steering can get hard to turn (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly takes much more effort, like a car with no power steering, often after left turns.
issues.why: The power steering pinion shaft could move inside the steering gear. GM recalled these vans to inspect it.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Wiper linkage can rub a brake line (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid loss, a soft pedal or longer stops.
issues.why: GM recalled these vans because the windshield wiper parts could rub through a brake line and leak fluid.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Van could roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The van might move after you think it is parked.
issues.why: GM recalled about 38,500 vans under the standard for gear shift and parking controls because the van could roll.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Always set the parking brake until it is checked.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not latch fully (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt may seem to latch but may not hold in a crash.
issues.why: GM recalled these vans for TRW seat belt buckles that might not restrain an occupant properly.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not be attached (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; a child seat clipped to the LATCH anchors may not be held properly.
issues.why: The child seat anchor wires on some vans were not attached correctly to the body.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Use the seat belt to install child seats until it is checked.

issues.t: Fuel tank inlet valve weld can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drips near the fuel filler side of the tank.
issues.why: The weld on the fuel tank inlet check valve could crack and let fuel vapor and drops escape, a fire risk.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Airbag inflator can break apart (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: GM recalled these vans because the airbag inflator could send fragments into the cabin and the bag might not fill fully.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not protect fully (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: GM recalled some 2003 vans because the driver airbag inflator could rupture and its pieces could hit people inside.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Parking brake may drag after release (recall)
issues.sym: A noise from the rear and the van feeling held back while driving after you release the parking brake.
issues.why: On some 2005 vans the parking brake lever could slip, so the brake stayed partly on after release.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Rear seat latches can release in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the rear seats may come loose in a severe side crash.
issues.why: GM recalled some 2005 vans because rear seat latches could let go too early in a severe side impact.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free.

issues.t: Tire label shows wrong load or pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The tire and loading sticker on the door frame lists incorrect information.
issues.why: A misprinted label could lead owners to overload the van or set tire pressure wrong.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup or call a GM dealer. If the work was never done, the dealer does it free. Until then, use the tire pressure shown in the owner's manual.
